payload.public_summary: The request is scientifically executable as stated: derive and check that differentiating x^2 with respect to x gives 2x. No blocking scientific ambiguities remain, so no frontier questions are needed this round.

specification_sections.name: purpose
specification_sections.content: Produce a self-contained derivation showing that d(x^2)/dx = 2x, and include an explicit check of the result.

specification_sections.name: scientific_target
specification_sections.content: The target quantity is the derivative of the function f(x)=x^2 with respect to x, with the result to be shown as 2x.

specification_sections.name: givens_and_starting_point
specification_sections.content: Given the user-specified function f(x)=x^2. Start from the textbook definition of the derivative with respect to x and carry out the algebra explicitly.

specification_sections.name: notation_and_conventions
specification_sections.content: Use standard calculus notation d(x^2)/dx and f'(x). Treat x as a real variable and h as the increment in the difference quotient.

specification_sections.name: assumptions_and_regime
specification_sections.content: Work in ordinary single-variable real calculus, at generic x where the derivative is defined. No distributional, complex-analytic, or numerical-approximation framework is required.

specification_sections.name: scope_and_non_goals
specification_sections.content: Scope: one elementary derivation and one explicit verification. Non-goals: extending to x^n, proving general power rules, or discussing alternative formalisms unless needed briefly for the check.

specification_sections.name: required_output
specification_sections.content: A checked derivation that explicitly differentiates x^2 with respect to x and concludes 2x, with the check stated in the output.

specification_sections.name: validation_criteria
specification_sections.content: The derivation must use valid algebra from the derivative definition, take the h->0 limit correctly, and include an explicit verification that the obtained derivative is 2x.

specification_sections.name: agent_discretion
specification_sections.content: The derivation agent may choose the specific check format, such as a direct substitution back into the difference quotient or a brief independent consistency check via the standard power rule, while keeping the main derivation elementary.

declared_defaults.title: Real-variable regime

declared_defaults.rationale: No user-stated constraint requires a broader regime, and this is the standard baseline for the requested result.

declared_defaults.title: Direct explicit check

declared_defaults.rationale: The user explicitly requested a checked derivation, and a direct check satisfies that requirement at minimal complexity.
